Stem says 'Storage is now the largest part of the bill'. The table-classes page says Standard-IA 'is the most cost-effective option for tables where storage is the dominant cost', so wrong option A (put the whole single table on Standard-IA) is defensible as a correct answer. Whether Standard-IA beats Standard for the whole table depends on unstated prices, not a documented property.
The why for wrong A relies on 'higher throughput cost' without the stem making throughput dominant for the active data.
suggestedFix: Remove the sentence 'Storage is now the largest part of the bill' and instead state that the current month takes nearly all the throughput while about 95 percent of the stored bytes sit in older months (keep it qualitative: 'most of the stored data is in older months, while almost all the throughput is on the current month'). Then wrong A fails because the active data would pay Standard-IA throughput rates, and the key is decidable from the documented Standard vs Standard-IA properties.
